A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 28-page versions of the EAGLET paper. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices can be matched reliably, including material relocated into the main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original EAGLET evaluations on ScienceWorld, ALFWorld and WebShop, alongside ablations, generalization tests, parameter analysis and a case study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results and supporting analyses in Section 4 and the reorganized appendices.

M1.justification: The planner–executor framework, cold-start SFT, homologous consensus filtering, executor capability gain reward, format reward and GRPO optimization remain unchanged in Sections 2–3.

E1.justification: Both versions use ScienceWorld, ALFWorld and WebShop with identical seen/unseen coverage and auxiliary task scenarios. No dataset, domain or evaluation task is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same LLMs, AgentTuning, ETO, GiGPO, WKM, KnowAgent, MPO and planner comparators. The citation additions in v2 do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, sample counts, reward and success metrics, prompting procedures, step limits, model configurations and training checkpoints are unchanged. The settings in v1 Appendix C are retained in v2 Appendix B.

E4.justification: The component ablations, executor variants, insertion-position tests, generalization analyses, plan-quality evaluation and case study are retained. The parameter study moves from v1 Appendix E/Table 10 to v2 Section 4.3/Table 8 without changing its analysis.

E5.justification: Both describe the same two planner generations and two executor runs per generated plan, plus two baseline runs or reused prior results. No seed information, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains averages of 88.1 for EAGLET + GPT-5 and 87.6 for EAGLET + GiGPO. The reordered appendix tables, Figure 4 percentages and case-study outcomes also match.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), including the trajectory formulation, filtering criterion, reward definitions and optimization objectives, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about a plug-and-play planner trained without manual effort, state-of-the-art results on three benchmarks and an eightfold training-efficiency advantage.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and limitations are retained, including text-only environments, executor availability, API training overhead and unexplored transfer across substantially different tasks. The parameter trade-off interpretation is relocated rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters, A100 hardware, checkpoint choices, API model identifiers and prompt templates remain unchanged. Implementation details move from Appendix C to B, and prompts from Appendix G to E.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including the emergent-abilities and chain-of-thought papers by Wei et al., RhinoInsight and FaithLens, while removing works including SANTA, SCL-RAI and MMICL. The substantive positioning against implicit and explicit planning methods remains unchanged; GATEAU's publication update is bibliographic.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Appendix A to Section 5, and the parameter study moves into Section 4.3, with corresponding appendix and cross-reference updates. v2 also edits author affiliations and correspondence information and adds acknowledgements; most prose is retained.

P2.justification: The parameter-study table moves into the main text as Table 8; the success-rate and variant tables become Tables 9 and 10. Figures and table content remain unchanged, with limited reflow, float relocation and removal of page-number footers.

improvement.justification: Moving the existing related-work discussion and parameter study into the main text makes research context and sensitivity evidence more accessible within the narrative. This is a limited organizational improvement: the methodology, empirical evidence, statistical support, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged.
